short: Reaching the same position by a different order of moves.
body: Openings are positions, not move lists. The same position can be reached half a dozen ways, which is why memorising a sequence is so much weaker than understanding what the position wants — a small change in move order and your list no longer applies.
It is also a practical weapon. Players use move orders to sidestep the lines their opponent has prepared, arriving at the same structure by a route the other person has not rehearsed.
This is why the app stores every lesson as a position index rather than a list of moves: reach the same position by another route and you land on the same explanation.

diagram.caption: The Wayward Queen has just transposed into Scholar's Mate — a different move order, the same threat.
